steps: Re-derive each of the 14 verdicts from the research lead at docs/agent-loops/whyknot-launch/research/l00-truth-table.md (written by this planning run; scratch fallback /Users/jay/.hermes/cache/scratch/whyknot-launch-L00-research.md) - a lead only, never a citation source: open each docs/roadmap/features/*.md for what it promises, then the code that would deliver it. Known correction to carry: the lead marks site-page-seo built although docs/roadmap/features/site-page-seo.md promises UTM click stats with no code, so the ladder regrades it.

Apply exactly one verdict per feature with this ladder (bottom to top: parked < spec only < partly built < built) and no compound verdicts: parked = deferred by a locked constraint or owner decision (constraint C4); spec only = no code implements any promised surface, where a presentational component appearing only in the design-system gallery does not count as code for the feature; partly built = at least one promised surface runs end to end in code and at least one promised surface has none; built = every promised surface in the feature md has working code (page, route, job or script), each cited. A row graded two ways takes the lower verdict.

Re-verify every file:line citation live before writing it - the working tree is dirty and stale line numbers are the main failure mode; never cite the research file itself; citations containing square brackets (dynamic routes like frontend/src/pages/sites/[slug].astro) do not count toward the 20-distinct-citation check, so include at least 20 citations without brackets.

risks: Dirty tree makes line numbers stale: every citation is re-read at build time, never copied from the research lead unverified.

Verdict drift: the roadmap status column is stale for all 14 rows, so the column is never the source - the feature md's promises against the code are; the ladder with its lower-verdict tie-break keeps two agents on the same table.
A doc that overstates readiness is a defect: anything not actually run is written as NOT RUN with the reason, including all eight gate rows while the box is blocked.

The checks pin structure, not truth: a row can satisfy the regex and still cite a wrong line, and the eight gate rows can in principle repeat a name - the build step's live re-verification and the pinned exact row names in step 4 are the real controls.
The screener deletion and the README column refresh are Jay's (gate 12): the file records them as open questions, it does not act on them.
